description: Retrieves a list of Shared Data by HTTP GET on the Shared Data Store resource using the sharedDataIdList query parameter.
normative_statements: The Service Consumer shall send an HTTP GET request to the "shared-data" store resource.
The request shall include the query parameter sharedDataIdList identifying the requested Shared Data.
On success, the NRF shall return 200 OK with the requested Shared Data in the response body.
If only a subset of the requested Shared Data is available or retrievable, the NRF shall still return 200 OK with the available and retrieved subset in the response body.
On failure, the NRF shall return a 4xx or 5xx response.
In case of redirection, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code with a Location header pointing to another NRF service instance.

constraints.statement: The Service Consumer shall send an HTTP GET request to the "shared-data" store resource.
evidence: The Service Consumer shall send an HTTP GET request to the resource URI "shared-data" store resource, where the query parameter sharedDataIdList identifies the requested Shared Data.
constraints.why_interesting: This fixes the HTTP method and target resource, which are directly testable at the API boundary.

constraints.statement: The request shall include the query parameter sharedDataIdList identifying the requested Shared Data.
evidence: The Service Consumer shall send an HTTP GET request to the resource URI "shared-data" store resource, where the query parameter sharedDataIdList identifies the requested Shared Data.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a required request parameter that can be validated by request inspection.

constraints.statement: On success, the NRF shall return 200 OK with the requested Shared Data in the response body.
evidence: On success, "200 OK" shall be returned with the requested Shared Data in response body.
constraints.why_interesting: This defines the success status code and required response payload behavior.

constraints.statement: If only a subset of the requested Shared Data is available or retrievable, the NRF shall still return 200 OK with the available and retrieved subset in the response body.
evidence: If only a subset of the requested Shared Data is available (locally stored or could be retrieved from a higher level NRF), the NRF shall still return "200 OK" with the available and retrieved subset of the requested Shared Data in the response body.
constraints.why_interesting: This is a non-obvious partial-success rule that affects observable status code and payload content.

constraints.statement: On failure, the NRF shall return a 4xx or 5xx response.
evidence: On failure, the NRF shall return "4xx/5xx" response and the response body may contain a ProblemDetails object describing the detailed information of the failure.
constraints.why_interesting: This constrains the failure status code class and is directly testable.

constraints.statement: In case of redirection, the NRF shall return a 3xx status code with a Location header pointing to another NRF service instance.
evidence: In the case of redirection, the NRF shall return 3xx status code, which shall contain a Location header with an URI pointing to the endpoint of another NRF service instance.
constraints.why_interesting: This specifies both the redirect status class and the required Location header.
